text: Chapter 5 is about controlling exactly which data reaches the view, and in what order. We'll start with the simplest three tools: sorting, basic filters, and quick filters.

Hover over an axis, a header, or a field label, and a small sort icon appears. Click it once to sort descending, click again for ascending, and a third click clears the sort back to its default order. Sorting never removes data — it only reorders what's already in the view.

A basic filter lives on the Filters shelf and is invisible to anyone viewing the finished chart — you have to open the workbook to change it. A quick filter takes that same filter and displays it as a live card directly on the view, so anyone looking at the dashboard can check or uncheck values themselves, no editing required.

Sort reorders marks without removing any data. A basic filter, dragged onto the Filters shelf, actually includes or excludes values from the view. And a quick filter takes that basic filter and surfaces it as an interactive card, right there on the sheet or dashboard.
Next lesson digs into the Filter dialog box itself — and how it behaves completely differently depending on whether you're filtering a dimension, a measure, or a date.
